title: Facet Joint Interventions: Medial Branch Blocks and Radiofrequency Neurotomy
description: Medicare coverage criteria for facet joint radiofrequency ablation (RFA/neurotomy). Requires chronic axial non-radicular pain >= 3 months, documented >= 80% pain relief from two separate diagnostic medial branch blocks (MBBs), and failure of conservative management.

criteria.name: Diagnostic Medial Branch Block Relief (>= 80%)
criteria.description: Documented >= 80% relief of target facet pain following dual diagnostic medial branch nerve blocks under fluoroscopic guidance.
criteria.clinical_intent: Validate facet joint as primary pain generator
criteria.source_text_excerpt: The Greater Manchester EUR Policy Statement on Facet Injections no longer commissioned IA facet injections and recommended medial branches nerve blocks for diagnostic evaluation for RFA 12 .

criteria.name: Chronic Axial Pain Duration (>= 3 Months)
criteria.description: Chronic non-radicular axial back or neck pain causing functional disability for >= 3 months (90 days).
criteria.clinical_intent: Confirm chronic duration of facet pain
criteria.source_text_excerpt: NASS Guidelines state that therapeutic medial branch RFA is a validated treatment for facet mediated pain, and repeat procedures are equally successful if the response to the initial RFA lasted at least three months.

criteria.name: Radiculopathy or Acute Fracture Exclusion
criteria.description: Primary pain due to radicular disc herniation, severe canal stenosis, acute compression fracture, or active tumor.
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Radiculopathy - Radiating neuropathic pain causally related to the spinal nerve root irritation, which extends distally producing neuropathic pain in a dermatomal pattern.
